ops.text: Three moving parts. First, a SIGTERM handler flips a readiness flag so /readyz returns 503 at once; this is the 'stop new traffic' step, and the process keeps serving while the load balancer stops routing to it. Second, the handler chains to uvicorn's own: uvicorn installs its signal handlers before it imports the app and runs the lifespan, so a handler that replaces them without chaining means uvicorn never starts its drain and the process waits for SIGKILL. In Example 21 the next signal (docker stop) goes to uvicorn, which stops accepting and finishes in-flight HTTP; --timeout-graceful-shutdown bounds that wait so a stuck request cannot hang the deploy. Third, FastAPI's lifespan shutdown block (after the yield) runs once HTTP has drained: that is where you stop consumers (an aiokafka consumer commits offsets and leaves the group) and close pools. The order matters: readiness down, drain HTTP, then drain everything else. Pair this with the preStop hook and the termination grace period in the pod spec.
